question: In India, 'National Science Day' is celebrated on February 28 to mark the achievement of which scientist?
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
solution_text:
The correct answer is C. V. Raman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Science Day (राष्ट्रीय विज्ञान दिवस) is observed every year on 28 February to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by Indian physicist Sir C. V. Raman on this day in 1928.

• For this discovery C. V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930, becoming the first Asian to receive a Nobel Prize in a science field.

• The day was first celebrated in 1987 after the National Council for Science and Technology Communication (NCSTC) proposed it in 1986.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Raman Effect deals with the scattering of light (inelastic scattering of photons) when it passes through a transparent medium.

• C. V. Raman was also awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954.

NOTE

• Homi J. Bhabha (Option 2): Known as the father of the Indian nuclear programme and founder of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR).

• Vikram Sarabhai (Option 3): Regarded as the father of the Indian space programme and the first chairman of ISRO.

• A. P. J. Abdul Kalam (Option 4): Missile scientist, 'Missile Man of India', and the 11th President of India.

question: In June 2025, who has become the first woman ADC (Aide-de-Camp) to the President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yashasvi Solanki.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, Lieutenant Commander Yashasvi Solanki of the Indian Navy became the first woman ADC (Aide-de-Camp / राष्ट्रपति की सहायक-शिविरपति) to the President of India, Droupadi Murmu.

• She is the first woman naval officer to be appointed to this ceremonial post.

• An Aide-de-Camp is a personal assistant/ceremonial officer to a high-ranking dignitary such as the President.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces and is assisted by ADCs drawn from the three services.

• This appointment is seen as a milestone in expanding roles for women in the Indian armed forces.

NOTE

• Neena Gupta (Option 1): A well-known Indian actress; also the name of a noted mathematician, but not the President's ADC.

• Aliawati Longkumer (Option 2): Not associated with this appointment.

• Anuradha Thakur (Option 4): Not associated with this appointment.

question: PM-YUVA 3.0 launched in March 2025 is related to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mentoring Young Authors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PM-YUVA 3.0 (प्रधानमंत्री युवा लेखक मेंटरशिप योजना) is the third edition of the PM Scheme for Mentoring Young Authors, launched in March 2025.

• Its aim is to train and mentor young/budding authors (below 30 years of age) to promote reading, writing and book culture in India.

• It is implemented by the National Book Trust (NBT) under the Ministry of Education.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• YUVA stands for Young, Upcoming and Versatile Authors.

• The scheme supports authors writing to showcase India, including themes on the unsung heroes of the freedom movement and Indian democracy.

NOTE

• Promoting Young Entrepreneurs (Option 2): Related to schemes like Startup India / Stand-Up India, not PM-YUVA.

• Providing Digital Literacy Training (Option 3): Covered under schemes like PMGDISHA.

• Healthcare Awareness Campaign (Option 4): Not the objective of PM-YUVA.

question: One Nation, One Subscription (ONOS) scheme, introduced on 1 January 2025 by which of the following ministry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Education.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The One Nation, One Subscription (ONOS) scheme (वन नेशन, वन सब्सक्रिप्शन योजना) was rolled out from 1 January 2025 by the Ministry of Education.

• It provides students, researchers and faculty of government higher educational institutions nationwide access to leading international scholarly journals through a single centralised subscription.

• It is coordinated through the Information and Library Network (INFLIBNET), an autonomous inter-university centre of the UGC.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme covers around 6,300+ government-run institutions including central and state universities, IITs, IIMs and colleges.

• It aims to democratise access to knowledge and boost research output across India.

NOTE

• Ministry of Finance (Option 2): Handles the Union Budget, taxation and economic policy, not this scheme.

• Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Option 3): Deals with trade, SEZs and industrial policy.

• Ministry of Heavy Industries (Option 4): Oversees capital goods and heavy engineering industries (e.g., automobiles, FAME scheme).

question: As per State of the Judiciary Report 2023, women constitute _____ of the working strength of the district judiciary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 36.3%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the State of the Judiciary Report 2023 (स्टेट ऑफ जुडिशियरी रिपोर्ट), prepared by the Centre for Research and Planning of the Supreme Court, women constitute about 36.3% of the working strength of the district judiciary.

• This figure highlights the growing but still limited representation of women in the lower judiciary.

• Representation of women falls sharply at higher levels (High Courts and the Supreme Court).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The report also flagged high vacancy levels in the district judiciary and infrastructure gaps such as lack of adequate toilets for women.

• The district judiciary is the base of India's three-tier judicial system.

NOTE

• 29.3% (Option 1): Not the reported figure for women in the district judiciary.

• 26.3% (Option 3): Incorrect figure.

• 46.3% (Option 4): Incorrect figure; overstates women's representation.

question: Which of the following species of big cat cannot roar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cheetah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given big cats, the Cheetah (चीता) is the one that cannot roar; instead it purrs, chirps and makes bird-like calls.

• Roaring big cats belong to the genus Panthera (lion, tiger, leopard, jaguar), whose special two-piece hyoid bone with an elastic ligament allows roaring.

• The cheetah (genus Acinonyx) has a fixed hyoid bone like small cats, so it can purr but not roar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching speeds of about 100–120 km/h.

• Cheetahs were reintroduced in India under Project Cheetah at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh (from 2022).

NOTE

• Leopard (Option 1): A member of genus Panthera and can roar.

• Tiger (Option 2): The largest cat of genus Panthera and can roar.

• Jaguar (Option 3): A Panthera species of the Americas that can roar.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Gopi Diaries: Finding Love'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sudha Murty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Gopi Diaries: Finding Love' is written by Sudha Murty (सुधा मूर्ति), a celebrated Indian author, educator and philanthropist.

• It is part of her popular 'The Gopi Diaries' trilogy for children, narrated from the perspective of a pet dog named Gopi.

• Sudha Murty writes in both English and Kannada, and her books are widely read by children and adults alike.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sudha Murty was the founder-chairperson of the Infosys Foundation and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2024.

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (2006) and Padma Bhushan (2023).

NOTE

• Rekha Verma (Option 2): Not the author of this book.

• Anuradha Roy (Option 3): An Indian novelist known for works like 'Sleeping on Jupiter'.

• Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni (Option 4): Indian-American author of 'The Palace of Illusions' and 'The Mistress of Spices'.

question: 'Adhratiya' is a traditional folk song of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Adhratiya' (अधरतिया) is a traditional folk song of the state of Jharkhand (झारखंड).

• It belongs to the rich tribal and folk music tradition of the region, sung on social and festive occasions.

• Jharkhand's folk music is closely tied to its tribal communities and seasonal festivals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other well-known folk songs/music forms of Jharkhand include Jhumar, Domkach, Faguwa and Paiki.

• Popular folk dances of Jharkhand include Chhau, Paika, Jhumair and Domkach.

NOTE

• Telangana (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Perini Shivatandavam and Bathukamma songs.

• Punjab (Option 3): Famous for Bhangra and Giddha folk traditions.

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Known for Lavani and Powada folk songs.

question: 'Baul' dance is performed in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Baul (बाउल) tradition of music and dance is associated with West Bengal (पश्चिम बंगाल) (and parts of Bangladesh).

• Bauls are wandering mystic minstrels who express devotion and spirituality through song and dance.

• Baul music was recognised by UNESCO in 2005 as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bauls are influenced by both Vaishnavism and Sufism and use instruments like the ektara, dotara and khamak.

• Other folk dances of West Bengal include Chhau, Gambhira and Dhali.

NOTE

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Known for Ghoomar and Kalbelia dances.

• Ladakh (Option 2): Known for the Cham (mask) dance.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for Lavani and Tamasha.

question: Who among the following was the first chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Vikram A Sarabhai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Vikram A. Sarabhai (डॉ. विक्रम ए. साराभाई) was the first chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), established in 1969.

• He is widely regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.

• He also founded the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) in Ahmedabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's first satellite, Aryabhata (1975), and the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station owe much to his vision.

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1966) and Padma Vibhushan (posthumously, 1972).

NOTE

• Prof. M G K Menon (Option 2): A physicist who briefly headed ISRO after Sarabhai's death, but was not the first chairman.

• Prof. Satish Dhawan (Option 3): The third chairman of ISRO, after whom the Sriharikota launch centre is named.

• Homi J Bhabha (Option 4): Father of the Indian nuclear programme, not ISRO's first chairman.

question: What happens to the pressure when the area is reduced while keeping the force same?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pressure increases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pressure (दाब) is defined as force per unit area: P = F / A.

• When the force (F) is kept constant and the area (A) is reduced, the pressure increases, because pressure is inversely proportional to area.

• This is why sharp objects (small area) exert greater pressure than blunt ones for the same force.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

• Examples: a knife's sharp edge, a needle's tip, and nails have small contact areas to increase pressure.

NOTE

• Pressure decreases (Option 1): Wrong; this happens when the area is increased for the same force.

• Pressure remains constant (Option 3): Wrong; pressure changes as area changes.

• Pressure becomes zero (Option 4): Wrong; pressure can never become zero while a force acts on a finite area.

question:
Which of the following statement about weight is correct?
I. Weight has only magnitude but no direction
II. Weight is a force acting vertically downwards
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Weight (भार) is the gravitational force exerted on a body: W = m × g, where m is mass and g is acceleration due to gravity.

• Being a force, weight is a vector quantity — it has both magnitude and direction, and it always acts vertically downwards (towards the centre of the Earth).

• Hence Statement II is correct, while Statement I (that weight has only magnitude and no direction) is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of weight is the newton (N), whereas mass is measured in kilograms (kg).

• Mass is a scalar and remains constant, but weight varies with the value of g at different locations.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, because Statement I is false — weight does have direction.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, since Statement I is incorrect.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong, since Statement II is correct.

question: Celonis and Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad (IIITA) have announced to launch a centre. Which of the following is one of the focus areas of the centre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Object-centric process mining.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Celonis and IIIT Allahabad (IIITA) jointly launched India's first Process Intelligence research centre, focusing on process mining technologies.

• One of the key focus areas of the centre is object-centric process mining (ऑब्जेक्ट-सेंट्रिक प्रोसेस माइनिंग), an advanced approach to analysing business processes.

• The collaboration aims to advance research, AI-driven process analytics and skill development in this field.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Celonis is a German company that pioneered the field of process mining / process intelligence.

• Process mining uses event-log data from IT systems to visualise and optimise real business processes.

NOTE

• A fashion design institute (Option 1): Unrelated to a process-intelligence/technology centre.

• A sports training academy (Option 2): Not the focus of this research centre.

• Semiconductor fab (Option 3): Relates to chip manufacturing, not process mining.

question: Which company developed the Gemini AI model?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Google.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gemini AI model (जेमिनी ए.आई. मॉडल) was developed by Google (through Google DeepMind).

• Gemini is a family of multimodal large language models, able to process text, images, audio, video and code.

• It was launched in December 2023 as a successor to Google's earlier models and as a competitor to systems like GPT.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Google DeepMind was formed by merging Google Brain and DeepMind.

• Gemini powers various Google products and comes in versions such as Ultra, Pro, Flash and Nano.

NOTE

• Apple (Option 1): Developed the AI framework 'Apple Intelligence' and Siri, not Gemini.

• Amazon (Option 2): Developed models like Amazon Titan/Nova and the Alexa assistant.

• IBM (Option 4): Known for Watson AI, not Gemini.

question: The National Pension System was launched in India in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2004.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Pension System (राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली) was launched in India in 2004.

• It was initially introduced for new central government employees (except armed forces) joining on or after 1 January 2004, replacing the old defined-benefit pension.

• From 1 May 2009, it was extended to all citizens on a voluntary basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The NPS is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

• It is a defined-contribution, market-linked pension scheme.

NOTE

• 1995 (Option 1): Year the EPFO's Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) was introduced, not NPS.

• 1998 (Option 2): Not the launch year of NPS.

• 2010 (Option 4): Incorrect; NPS predates this year.

question: In which year Guru Gobind Singh died?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1708.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Gobind Singh (गुरु गोबिंद सिंह), the tenth Sikh Guru, died in 1708 at Nanded (in present-day Maharashtra).

• He was born in 1666 at Patna and became Guru in 1675 after the martyrdom of his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur.

• Before his death he ended the line of human Gurus, declaring the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi.

• He instituted the five Ks (Panj Kakaar) for the Khalsa.

NOTE

• 1711 (Option 2): Not the year of his death.

• 1718 (Option 3): Incorrect year.

• 1722 (Option 4): Incorrect year.

question: In India, the SEZs Rules, 2006 came into effect in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is February, 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Rules, 2006 (एस.ई.जेड. नियम, 2006) came into effect in February 2006 (from 10 February 2006).

• They operationalised the SEZ Act, 2005, providing the framework for setting up and running SEZs.

• SEZs are duty-free enclaves treated as foreign territory for trade operations, duties and tariffs, to boost exports and investment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SEZs offer incentives like tax holidays, simplified procedures and single-window clearance.

• India's first SEZ concept drew from the earlier Export Processing Zones (EPZs), the first being at Kandla (1965).

NOTE

• November, 2006 (Option 1): Not when the SEZ Rules came into force.

• June, 2006 (Option 3): Incorrect date.

• September, 2006 (Option 4): Incorrect date.

question: The minimum age to vote in Indian State Legislative Election is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The minimum age to vote (मतदान की न्यूनतम आयु) in Indian elections, including State Legislative Assembly elections, is 18 years.

• This is based on universal adult suffrage guaranteed under Article 326 of the Constitution.

• The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A person must be at least 18 years of age on the qualifying date to be enrolled as a voter.

• The minimum age to contest a Legislative Assembly election is 25 years.

NOTE

• 16 years (Option 1): Below the constitutional voting age.

• 21 years (Option 3): Was the voting age before the 1988 amendment.

• 25 years (Option 4): The minimum age to contest (not vote in) an Assembly election.

question: The AMUL milk cooperative was established in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The AMUL milk cooperative (अमूल दूध सहकारी समिति) was established in the state of Gujarat, at Anand, in 1946.

• It was founded as the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union under the leadership of Tribhuvandas Patel, with Dr. Verghese Kurien later steering its growth.

• AMUL stands for Anand Milk Union Limited.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• AMUL is managed by the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF).

• It triggered the White Revolution (Operation Flood), making India the world's largest milk producer; Dr. Verghese Kurien is called the 'Father of the White Revolution'.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 1): Home to the Sudha dairy brand, not AMUL.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Associated with the Aavin dairy brand.

• Kerela (Option 4): Associated with the Milma dairy brand.

question: Which of the following five year plan in India tried to build the basis for a socialist pattern of society?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Second Five Year Plan (दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना) (1956–61) aimed to build the basis for a socialist pattern of society.

• It was based on the Mahalanobis model and emphasised rapid industrialisation, especially heavy and basic industries in the public sector.

• It reflected the objective set by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The plan led to the setting up of steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur.

• Its main architect was statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.

NOTE

• First (Option 1): The First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture and irrigation.

• Tenth (Option 3): The Tenth Plan (2002–07) targeted 8% GDP growth and reduction of poverty.

• Eleventh (Option 4): The Eleventh Plan (2007–12) focused on 'faster and more inclusive growth'.

question: The first industrial policy of Government of India was announced in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1948.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Industrial Policy (पहली औद्योगिक नीति) of the Government of India was announced in 1948.

• It was presented by the then Industry Minister Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.

• It laid down a mixed economy framework, envisaging roles for both the public and private sectors and classifying industries accordingly.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It was followed by the landmark Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, which gave the public sector a dominant role.

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991 ushered in liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG reforms).

NOTE

• 1947 (Option 1): The year of independence, but the first industrial policy came a year later.

• 1958 (Option 3): Not the year of the first industrial policy.

• 1964 (Option 4): Incorrect year.

question: There are mainly _____ main processes of change of population.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There are mainly three (3) processes of change of population (जनसंख्या परिवर्तन की प्रक्रियाएँ): births, deaths and migration.

• Births (fertility) and deaths (mortality) together determine the natural growth of population.

• Migration (movement of people in and out of an area) is the third factor affecting population change.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Crude Birth Rate (CBR) and Crude Death Rate (CDR) are measured per 1,000 population.

• Migration can be internal (within a country) or international, and can be measured as immigration and emigration.

NOTE

• 5 (Option 2): Not the number of main processes of population change.

• 6 (Option 3): Incorrect number.

• 7 (Option 4): Incorrect number.

question: The sum of the gross value added of all the firms in an economy in a year is called _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross Domestic Product.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sum of the Gross Value Added (GVA) of all firms in an economy in a year is called the Gross Domestic Product (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद).

• GDP measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory in a year.

• GDP at basic prices = sum of GVA of all producing units.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• GDP (at market prices) = GVA + Product Taxes − Product Subsidies.

• GDP can be measured by three methods: production (value-added), income and expenditure.

NOTE

• Net National Product (Option 2): NNP = GNP − depreciation; a net national aggregate, not the simple sum of firms' GVA.

• Gross Disposable Income (Option 3): Income available to residents for consumption and saving, not a production measure.

• Net National Income (Option 4): NNP at factor cost; the national income after adjusting for depreciation and net factor income from abroad.

question: Which of the following hormone is associated with puberty in human males?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Testosterone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Testosterone (टेस्टोस्टेरॉन) is the male sex hormone associated with puberty in human males.

• It is secreted by the testes (Leydig cells) and controls the development of secondary sexual characters such as facial hair, deepening of voice and muscle growth.

• It also regulates sperm production (spermatogenesis).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Testosterone is an androgen, a steroid hormone whose secretion is stimulated by Luteinising Hormone (LH) from the pituitary gland.

• The corresponding female sex hormones are oestrogen and progesterone.

NOTE

• Adrenaline (Option 1): The 'emergency/fight-or-flight' hormone secreted by the adrenal medulla.

• Oestrogen (Option 2): The primary female sex hormone responsible for female secondary sexual characters.

• Thyroxin (Option 3): A hormone of the thyroid gland that regulates metabolism (contains iodine).

question: Most of Ashoka's edicts were composed in which language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prakrit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Most of Ashoka's edicts (अशोक के अभिलेख) were composed in the Prakrit language.

• They were mostly written in the Brahmi script, while some north-western edicts used the Kharoshthi, Aramaic and Greek scripts/languages.

• The edicts spread the message of Dhamma (moral and ethical conduct) across the Mauryan Empire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ashoka's inscriptions were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

• The edicts include Major and Minor Rock Edicts, Pillar Edicts and Cave inscriptions.

NOTE

• Pali (Option 1): The language of Buddhist canonical texts (Tripitaka), but not the main language of Ashoka's edicts.

• Arabic (Option 2): A much later language, not used in Ashoka's edicts.

• English (Option 4): A modern language, entirely unrelated to the ancient Mauryan period.
